newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares close down as investors wait.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares close down as investors wait.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B shares fell slightly on Wednesday as investors waited for new incentives to enter the market to buy, brokers said.
Investors were waiting to buy new issues and looking towards 1997 interim results, which listed companies must report by the end of August, they said.
The B index ended the day down 0.317 points or 0.42 percent to 74.522 points on volume of 10.962 million shares worth $4.596 million.
"There's no news and foreign institutions haven't returned to the market," said an analyst from China Guotai Securities.
"There are some pending new issues so people don't have an interest in buying existing shares," he said.
Only one B share firm, material maker Shanghai Haixin Co, had announced 1997 interim results and investors were also waiting for more earnings reports, brokers said.
Listed companies are required to announce interim results before the end of August, but poorly performing firms usually wait until shortly before the deadline.
The B index fluctuated in a narrow range of 74.522 points to 75.364 points on Wednesday, ending in negative territory after the domestic currency A share market fell toward the close, brokers said.
The Shanghai A index lost ground in line with losses in Shenzhen's domestic currency shares, which fell on selling of market leader Shenzhen Development Bank, they said.

Investors had expected the bank to perform better when it resumed trading on Wednesday afternoon, after announcing its 1996 dividend plan would be unchanged despite heavy fines by regulators for illegal trading of its own shares.
Of 45 B shares, 37 traded with 17 down, 17 up and three flat.
Shanghai Sanmao Textiles Co was the biggest B share loser on speculative selling, plunging $0.010 or 7.14 percent to $0.130.
Brokers said shares of property developers with ties to Shanghai's Pudong development zone also came under selling pressure.
Shanghai Refrigerator Compressor Co was the most actively traded B share on bargain-hunting, inching up $0.002 or 0.50 percent to $0.402 on volume of around 1.3 million shares.
The A index lost 9.942 points or 0.79 percent to 1,254.619 points on volume of 462.101 million shares worth 5.424 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index fell 36.153 points or 0.94 percent to 3,821.340 points.
Both A and B shares were likely to stay around current levels on Thursday, brokers said.
"The market will stay balanced if there is no fresh news in the short term," a local broker said.
